offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 23rd of 32.
offence.blurb: Threw the ball more often than any other team last season, though without much yardage per attempt; Trey McBride and Marvin Harrison Jr. are the targets, with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback now that Kyler Murray is starting in Minnesota, and Jeremiyah Love arriving as the third overall pick.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 29th of 32.
defence.blurb: Rarely gets to the quarterback, and doesn't force many turnovers either. Josh Sweat, who came from Philadelphia, leads the rush, and the cornerback spots lean on two very recent draft picks in Will Johnson and Denzel Burke.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 30th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chad Ryland's place-kicking, with one of the better field-goal rates in the league, is the dependable part here; Devin Duvernay, who came from Baltimore, handles kick returns.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 24th of 32.
offence.blurb: Runs the ball noticeably more than most teams, built around Bijan Robinson, while the passing game under Tua Tagovailoa reached the end zone rarely despite Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 19th of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets after the quarterback about as well as anyone in the league and takes the ball away often, with a rotation of pass rushers rather than one star, and A.J. Terrell Jr. leading the cornerbacks.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 24th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Veteran Nick Folk handles the kicking and has been reliable on field goals; Zachariah Branch, a third-round pick, takes the kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 11th of 32.
offence.blurb: Passed less often than any team in the league, and ran for more yards per carry than anyone, with Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson's own frequent runs both central to it.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 18th of 32.
defence.blurb: Doesn't sack the quarterback much despite Trey Hendrickson, who came from New Orleans, and veteran Calais Campbell up front; Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins cover at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 12th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Young kicker Tyler Loop, a sixth-round pick, has been accurate on field goals, with Rasheen Ali returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 4th of 32.
offence.blurb: Josh Allen is a huge part of the running game himself, carrying it far more than most quarterbacks, and the unit scored more rushing touchdowns than anyone; new head coach Joe Brady was promoted from within after Sean McDermott's firing, so last year's run-leaning mix may not hold.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 12th of 32.
defence.blurb: Neither sacks the quarterback nor takes the ball away especially often. Bradley Chubb, who came from Denver, rushes the passer, and the cornerbacks are Christian Benford and first-round pick Maxwell Hairston.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 8th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Tyler Bass makes field goals at one of the highest rates in the league, and Ray Davis handles kick returns, under new head coach Joe Brady.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 27th of 32.
offence.blurb: Built around former first overall pick Bryce Young, with rookie first-rounder Tetairoa McMillan and Chuba Hubbard around him. Yards per pass throw was among the lowest in the league, and touchdowns on the ground were scarce.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 15th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that takes the ball away at a decent clip but rarely gets to the quarterback. Derrick Brown anchors the middle, Jaycee Horn the outside, with Jaelan Phillips having arrived from Miami.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 22nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Ryan Fitzgerald has been reliable on field goals, one of the better accuracy marks in the league. Rookie fourth-rounder Trevor Etienne handles kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 9th of 32.
offence.blurb: Under Ben Johnson this group ran the ball efficiently and protected it better than anyone else in the league. Caleb Williams is a real part of the running game himself, with young pass-catchers Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland around him.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 23rd of 32.
defence.blurb: A ball-hawking group that took the ball away more often than any other team, though sacks were harder to come by. Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson man the corners, with Montez Sweat rushing off the edge.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 18th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Veteran kicker Cairo Santos was among the most accurate on field goals; Zavion Thomas, a recent third-round pick, takes kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 12th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most pass-heavy attacks in football, throwing far more often than the typical team, with Joe Burrow feeding Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Passing touchdowns came in bunches; the running game gained little per carry.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 30th of 32.
defence.blurb: A young secondary of Dax Hill and DJ Turner II, with Boye Mafe having come from Seattle to rush the edge. Pressure on the quarterback has been hard to find.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 9th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Evan McPherson is the centrepiece, converting field goals at one of the league's better rates, with Charlie Jones returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 31st of 32.
offence.blurb: A young, rebuilt group leaning on rookie-contract pieces like Quinshon Judkins, Harold Fannin Jr. and first-round picks KC Concepcion and Spencer Fano. Yards per pass attempt were the lowest in the league, and Deshaun Watson remains the man at quarterback.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 14th of 32.
defence.blurb: A pass-rushing group that piled up sacks, though it forces few turnovers. Myles Garrett has since been traded to the Rams for picks, leaving Alex Wright, Jared Verse and cornerbacks Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell to carry it.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 10th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Andre Szmyt has been accurate on field goals, with Malachi Corley, who came from the Jets, taking kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 7th of 32.
offence.blurb: A pass-first group built around Dak Prescott throwing to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, who came from Pittsburgh; they threw for touchdowns often but gave the ball away more than most.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 32nd of 32.
defence.blurb: A front with two established interior linemen in Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, but a unit that rarely forces fumbles or interceptions; veteran pass rusher Von Miller has agreed to a one-year deal.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 16th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built around kicker Brandon Aubrey, who was among the most accurate in the league on field goals, with KaVontae Turpin handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 14th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw more than nearly anyone, with Bo Nix also carrying the ball himself a lot, though the passing gained few yards per attempt; Jaylen Waddle came from Miami.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 3rd of 32.
defence.blurb: Sacked the quarterback more than any other team, led by Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, with Pat Surtain II at cornerback — but they take the ball away rarely.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 14th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Wil Lutz was among the league's most accurate on field goals, and Marvin Mims Jr. handles the kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 5th of 32.
offence.blurb: A balanced group under Dan Campbell that scores through the air with Jared Goff, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta, while Jahmyr Gibbs runs behind Penei Sewell; they hold onto the ball well.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 22nd of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets after the quarterback often with Aidan Hutchinson leading the rush, but doesn't create many turnovers behind him.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 27th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicker Jake Bates and returner Jacob Saylors are the names here; the field-goal kicking has been the more dependable part.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 16th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-leaning offences in the league, handing off to Josh Jacobs, though Jordan Love's throws to Tucker Kraft and company gained big yards; they almost never turn it over.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 11th of 32.
defence.blurb: Built around Micah Parsons, who came from Dallas, alongside interior linemen Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks; sacks and takeaways were both hard to come by last season.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 23rd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: A young group with rookie sixth-round kicker Trey Smack and Skyy Moore, who came from Kansas City, returning kicks.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 13th of 32.
offence.blurb: Built around C.J. Stroud throwing to Nico Collins, with a split between run and pass right at the league norm. Gained little on the ground, but gave the ball away less than almost anyone; Jayden Higgins and tackle Aireontae Ersery are recent first-two-round picks.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 2nd of 32.
defence.blurb: DeMeco Ryans' defence gets after the quarterback through Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter, and takes the ball away about as often as any team, with Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 6th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Rests on Ka'imi Fairbairn, who made better than nine in ten of his field goals, with rookie draft pick Jaylin Noel handling kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 8th of 32.
offence.blurb: Runs through Jonathan Taylor, who helped them score more rushing touchdowns than nearly any team, with Daniel Jones (a former Giants first-rounder) throwing to Alec Pierce, Josh Downs and rookie tight end Tyler Warren.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 21st of 32.
defence.blurb: Leans on its cornerbacks, Sauce Gardner, who came from the Jets, and Charvarius Ward, and gets a decent number of takeaways; the pass rush around Laiatu Latu is less of a factor.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 2nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Anchored by Blake Grupe, who missed barely any field goals all year, with Anthony Gould returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 6th of 32.
offence.blurb: Trevor Lawrence is a big part of the running game himself, carrying the ball more than most quarterbacks, and Brian Thomas Jr. is the main target. They found the end zone on the ground often despite short average gains.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 8th of 32.
defence.blurb: A takeaway machine — few teams intercepted and forced more fumbles — but it rarely sacks the quarterback despite Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen up front. Travis Hunter plays both sides of the ball.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 13th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicker Cam Little, a late-round pick of theirs, was reliable, and running back Bhayshul Tuten doubles as the kick returner.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 21st of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most pass-heavy attacks in the league under Andy Reid, with Patrick Mahomes throwing to Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce, and Mahomes running a fair bit himself. Kenneth Walker III, formerly of Seattle, carries the load on the ground.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 6th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that neither sacks the quarterback nor forces turnovers often, relying instead on coverage — and it has just lost All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie in a trade to the Rams, with a top-six pick at the position brought in behind L'Jarius Sneed.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 15th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built around veteran kicker Harrison Butker, who came from Carolina, with Nikko Remigio returning kicks.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 20th of 32.
offence.blurb: Throws more than most teams, with Justin Herbert also carrying the ball himself a good deal; Ladd McConkey and first-round rookie back Omarion Hampton are the other pieces, though touchdowns on the ground were hard to come by.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 9th of 32.
defence.blurb: A front built around Khalil Mack, who came from Oakland, that both gets to the quarterback and takes the ball away at a decent clip, with Cam Hart and Donte Jackson at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 5th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking is the strength here: Cameron Dicker made a higher share of his field goals than any other kicker, with Derius Davis handling kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 1st of 32.
offence.blurb: Matthew Stafford threw for more touchdowns than any other quarterback and the ball rarely gets given away, with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams outside and Kyren Williams keeping the run and pass split even.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 10th of 32.
defence.blurb: A pass rush of Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske and Myles Garrett, who arrived in a trade from Cleveland, plus cornerback Trent McDuffie, traded in from Kansas City — pressure and takeaways are both regular features.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 28th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Harrison Mevis has been accurate on field goals and Jordan Whittington returns kicks, but the return and coverage work has not matched the kicking.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 32nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Klint Kubiak takes over, so last year's pass-heavy split belongs to the old staff; the ground game gained less per carry than anyone's, and the rebuild leans on rookie back Ashton Jeanty, tight end Brock Bowers and new record-paid centre Tyler Linderbaum in front of Kirk Cousins.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 25th of 32.
defence.blurb: Under new head coach Klint Kubiak, a group that doesn't force many turnovers, with Kwity Paye and Eric Stokes, both of whom came from elsewhere, alongside rookie corner Darien Porter.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 25th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Matt Gay, who came from Tampa Bay, handles the kicking and has been reliable on field goals, with receiver Tre Tucker doubling up on kick returns.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 25th of 32.
offence.blurb: Runs a bit more than most teams and gains more per carry than almost anyone through De'Von Achane, but gave the ball away often and now hands the job to Malik Willis after Tua Tagovailoa was released.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 24th of 32.
defence.blurb: Built around young edge rushers Chop Robinson and Josh Uche, with a very inexperienced cornerback group in Jason Marshall Jr. and JuJu Brents, who came from Indianapolis.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 4th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Riley Patterson has been one of the most accurate kickers in the league, and Malik Washington doubles as the kick returner.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 26th of 32.
offence.blurb: Built around Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson, though the ball didn't travel far per throw and Minnesota gave it away more than any other team. Kyler Murray has now been named starter ahead of J.J. McCarthy.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 7th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that gets after the quarterback about as well as anyone, with first-round linebacker Dallas Turner and a corner group of Isaiah Rodgers and James Pierre that nobody drafted highly.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 3rd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Runs through kicker Will Reichard, who made a higher share of his field goals than any other kicker in the league, with Myles Price handling returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 2nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Gained more per pass than any offence in football, and Drake Maye is a real part of the running game himself, carrying it around a hundred times. A.J. Brown arrives by trade from Philadelphia to join Hunter Henry and rookie tackle Will Campbell.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 4th of 32.
defence.blurb: Rarely gets to the quarterback and doesn't take the ball away often; the strength is the cornerback pairing of Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III, plus interior linemen Christian Barmore and Milton Williams, who came from Philadelphia.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 19th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Very young: rookie kicker Andy Borregales, who converted a high share of his attempts, and fellow rookie Kyle Williams returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 28th of 32.
offence.blurb: Throws more than most teams, partly because the running game went nowhere — only one team averaged less per carry. Chris Olave and top-ten pick Jordyn Tyson are the targets, with second-year quarterback Tyler Shough and Travis Etienne Jr., who came from Jacksonville.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 16th of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets to the quarterback at a good rate with veteran ends Cameron Jordan and Chase Young, the latter from Washington, behind a young corner pair of Kool-Aid McKinstry and Quincy Riley.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 32nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Undrafted kicker Charlie Smyth missed a fair share of his field goals, and rookie Barion Brown takes the kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 17th of 32.
offence.blurb: Scored plenty of rushing touchdowns but few through the air, and quarterback Jaxson Dart is a big part of the run game himself alongside rookie back Cam Skattebo. Malik Nabers is the main target.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 26th of 32.
defence.blurb: Takes the ball away less often than almost anyone, and is being rebuilt around very recent picks in Abdul Carter and Darius Alexander, with corners Paulson Adebo and Greg Newsome II arriving from New Orleans and Cleveland.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 11th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Undrafted kicker Ben Sauls made a higher share of his field goals than anyone in the league, while first-round cornerback Deonte Banks doubles up as the kick returner.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 29th of 32.
offence.blurb: A unit that got much more out of running than throwing last year — solid yards per carry behind Breece Hall, near the bottom in yards per pass and passing touchdowns with Geno Smith. Garrett Wilson is the main target, with first-round tight end Kenyon Sadiq just added.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 31st of 32.
defence.blurb: A group that almost never takes the ball away — fewest takeaways in the league — and rarely gets to the quarterback. Will McDonald IV leads the rush, with corners Nahshon Wright and Brandon Stephens, who came from Dallas and Baltimore.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 1st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built on kicking accuracy: Jason Sanders, who came from Miami, made a higher share of his field goals than any other kicker, with Kene Nwangwu handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 19th of 32.
offence.blurb: Jalen Hurts is a big part of the running game himself, carrying the ball far more often than most quarterbacks, alongside Saquon Barkley. With A.J. Brown traded to New England, DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert are the main receiving options.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 5th of 32.
defence.blurb: Built around Jalen Carter inside and Jonathan Greenard rushing off the edge, with young corner Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen, who came from Seattle, in coverage. Gets after the quarterback and takes the ball away at a healthy rate.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 31st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jake Elliott, who came from Cincinnati, makes a high share of his field goals, so whatever holds this unit back is not the kicking. Will Shipley returns kicks.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 15th of 32.
offence.blurb: Throws a little more than the average team, with Aaron Rodgers rarely running himself and DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. — both arrived from elsewhere — as the targets. Plenty of passing touchdowns, but not many yards per throw.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 17th of 32.
defence.blurb: A pressure-and-turnover group: among the league leaders in both sacks and takeaways, with Cameron Heyward and Alex Highsmith up front and Joey Porter Jr. at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 20th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chris Boswell handles the kicking at a middling accuracy rate, with rookie fourth-round pick Kaden Wetjen taking over on kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 3rd of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the least pass-heavy teams in the league last year, yet nearly nobody gained more per throw — Sam Darnold hitting Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Rashid Shaheed on big plays rather than churning out yards on the ground with Zach Charbonnet.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 1st of 32.
defence.blurb: Mike Macdonald's group gets to the quarterback and takes the ball away often, with Leonard Williams and Jarran Reed inside. Devon Witherspoon has been locked up long-term and Terrion Arnold added at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 17th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jason Myers is among the most accurate kickers in the league, and Rashid Shaheed doubles as the kick returner.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 10th of 32.
offence.blurb: Throws a bit less than most teams and gets very little from its runs, but scores through the air with Brock Purdy finding George Kittle, Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans, who came from Tampa Bay. Christian McCaffrey arrived from Carolina.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 13th of 32.
defence.blurb: Got to the quarterback less often than any other team last season and rarely forced turnovers, so much rests on young pass rusher Mykel Williams, a first-round pick, alongside Osa Odighizuwa from Dallas.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 7th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built around kicker Eddy Pineiro, who made a higher share of his field goals than anyone in the league, with Isaac Guerendo handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 18th of 32.
offence.blurb: Splits run and pass about as evenly as the typical team, leaning on Bucky Irving on the ground while Baker Mayfield throws to Chris Godwin and first-round rookie Emeka Egbuka; Mayfield also runs a fair amount himself.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 20th of 32.
defence.blurb: Takes the ball away more than most teams under Todd Bowles, with a young cornerback pair in Zyon McCollum and second-round pick Benjamin Morrison and Yaya Diaby rushing off the edge.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 21st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chase McLaughlin is reliable on field goals, and Kenny Gainwell, who came from Philadelphia, handles kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 30th of 32.
offence.blurb: Passed on a bigger share of plays than almost any team while gaining little per throw, and it is now shaped around first overall pick Cam Ward and fellow high pick Carnell Tate, with Tony Pollard running.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 28th of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets after the quarterback reasonably often through John Franklin-Myers and Jermaine Johnson, who came from the Rams and Jets, but it forces very few turnovers behind a cornerback group assembled from elsewhere.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 26th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Joey Slye takes the kicks and rookie fourth-round pick Chimere Dike returns them.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 22nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Leans on the run more than almost anyone and gains plenty per carry, with Jayden Daniels himself a big part of that on the ground; Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, who came from Minnesota, are the targets.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 27th of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets home on the pass rush at a decent rate but almost never takes the ball away, with young cornerbacks Trey Amos and Mike Sainristil behind a front including Javon Kinlaw, who came from San Francisco.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 29th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking duties sit with Drew Stevens, and Luke McCaffrey, a third-round pick, brings back kicks.
